Odin × Godot

Box3D editor, bake artifacts and debug drawing

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Editor and runtime boundariesDetached artifactsCopied debug geometryEvidence scopeShared artifact APIDebug data bridgeProject setup and editor workflow

P5.3 builds tools around the shared authoring contract. It does not introduce a physics scheduler, a network protocol or a second rollback runtime. The declared macOS reference passes 18 standalone checks and the actual SDK editor/runtime fixture. Exact artifacts and limits are in the task report.

Editor and runtime boundaries#

The optional addon uses normal Godot inspector and 3D gizmo plugins. Authoring nodes and Resources retain their explicit stable keys and rigid-transform rules. Previews and validation warnings do not become canonical Game/Side. Property editing and plugin enable/disable must use normal editor ownership and cleanup.

Mesh conversion reads actual Mesh/ArrayMesh arrays once, validates triangle and index data, copies geometry and records version/source metadata. Shared baking still owns canonical geometry, IDs, deduplication and native limits. A preview must not silently discard unsupported surfaces, invalid transforms, sensor flags or capacity overflow.

Detached artifacts#

Bake artifacts are versioned owning authoring data. They must preserve the shared semantic bake identity, source/import metadata and exact integer IDs. Godot-facing payloads keep wide IDs opaque or hexadecimal; JSON floats cannot be used to roundtrip arbitrary u64 identities. Loaders bound input length and validate schema, version, integrity, references and field values before publishing an owner. Source nodes, Resources and files can disappear after successful load.

The ordinary SDK supports reusable tool scripts under res://modules/<name>. If the editor bridge needs one, install it once per project and build it through the existing module workflow. A missing tool bridge should be an actionable setup state. It does not justify a Core loader workaround or per-scene simulation code. Runtime import/bake goes through the same shared implementation.

Copied debug geometry#

Debug drawing is optional and defaults off at runtime. Its source is immutable authored geometry plus copied public presentation/checkpoint values. Kit and Replay retain their separate presentation readers and feed one common line data contract. A draw operation never queries a live solver or reads a Godot Resource during resimulation.

Line generation is bounded and validates inputs before output publication. Epoch, tick and revision remain explicit so stale drawing can be rejected or cleared. Drawing owns no tick or wall clock and never changes input, admission, effects or canonical state. The existing Native-free and Godot-free value presentation package keeps that boundary.

Evidence scope#

Completion requires pure artifact/geometry/integrity/ownership controls, real Mesh and Resource/scene roundtrips, source-free construction, ordinary SDK import, actual editor plugin registration and teardown, and drawing from copied Kit and Replay values with no Native allocation or canonical mutation. Headless component checks do not establish a manual pixel/usability review. Export Gate C remains a separate task.

Shared artifact API#

godot:box3d/authoring exposes artifact_create, artifact_load and artifact_destroy. The owning envelope retains exact definition bytes and source/import metadata, the semantic baked identity and the shared bake source fingerprint. Loading validates the bounded versioned envelope and invokes the same parser/baker again. It does not deserialize native solver layouts.

Odin
artifact, problem := a.artifact_create(definition_bytes,
    a.import_metadata(source_uri, source_revision), allocator)
if problem.error != .None {return}
defer a.artifact_destroy(&artifact)

loaded, load_problem := a.artifact_load(artifact.encoded, allocator)
if load_problem.error != .None {return}
defer a.artifact_destroy(&loaded)
// loaded owns an independent immutable scene; use the ordinary a.build path.

The reusable AuthoringTools tool module exposes exactly three editor methods: inspect_definition_json, bake_definition_json and inspect_artifact_base64. Inspection reports wide IDs as fixed hexadecimal strings. Its preview is explicitly an authored shape outline, without a runtime frame or invented stamp. Joint/character gizmos use their separately identified authored inputs. Preview failure and capacity are reported explicitly.

Debug data bridge#

box3d/debugdraw.generate consumes a copied presentation Frame, copied geometry bindings and an exact expected epoch/tick/revision/source. Generation is pure, allocation-free and all-or-failure. authoring.debug_scene_create copies the geometry and local maps so they can outlive the bake, native world and source framework; current character overlays must come from actual Game/Side values. authoring.debug_preview uses the same outline helpers for authored shapes.

godot:box3d/godot/debugdraw.frame_json copies a successful line batch into an owning JSON payload for the optional renderer. Epoch, tick and revision are 16-character lowercase hexadecimal strings. Endpoints and per-line colors are bounded finite arrays. Delete returned bytes with the same allocator. This serialization helper calls no Godot or Native API.

Project setup and editor workflow#

Copy the box3d_authoring addon into the project. Use its install action once to copy the packaged tools source into res://modules/box3d_authoring_tools, then run the normal Odin script/module build. The installer accepts identical existing files and refuses to overwrite a different project module. Enable the standard res://addons/box3d_authoring/plugin.cfg editor plugin after the build.

Select an authored World/body/shape, character/joint setting, MeshInstance or bake artifact to use its Inspector panel. The normal exported property editors remain active. Validation/inspection uses the shared tool module and reports field diagnostics and hexadecimal identities. World baking saves the checked owning artifact; Mesh baking requires an explicit stable shape key and copies actual surface vertices/indices into a Mesh shape Resource. Source affine transforms are baked, including corrected triangle winding for reflection. Skinned/blend-shape sources, non-triangle surfaces, invalid transforms and unsupported mesh sensor flags report errors. Render-only UV/normal/tangent data is not collision identity.

The registered artifact importer handles .b3authoring envelopes, waits for real filesystem reimport completion and saves a normal Resource carrying the Box3DBakeArtifact script. Its declared loader type is the native Resource; the loaded instance still has to satisfy the expected script class and strict shared artifact validation. Derived addon classes name their registered parent classes so the editor has a valid native-base/icon fallback.

The optional Box3DDebugDraw3D consumes explicit detached line batches. Enable it in presentation code and call submit_frame_json(payload, expected_stamp); its default is off, and stale batches clear prior drawing. Rendering uses an ImmediateMesh and does not schedule physics or query a solver. Preview limits are eight geometries, 35 bindings, one joint, 35 character overlays, 4096 mesh vertices/triangles and 8192 lines. Preview Capacity is explicit and never raises simulation limits or publishes a truncated shape.

The SDK fixture observed registered Inspector and gizmo callbacks, actual edited Resource property changes, artifact reimport and plugin disable/reenable. It also built and stepped the exact imported ArrayMesh artifact after source destruction, then rendered actual detached Kit and Replay batches without changing Native allocation totals. These are headless API/geometry checks; a manual pixel and usability review is outside this result. Export Gate C remains open.
